title: "Many Are My Names": The Anatomy of the Assistant and Its Personas via Sparse Autoencoders
abstract: arXiv:2608.07852v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: How a language model internally represents who is speaking, the Assistant, an assigned roleplay persona, or a narrated story character, remains underexplored. We study speaker representations using a dataset of user-expressed emotional text and corresponding model responses. We decompose three generation settings (Assistant, Roleplay, and Story) into sparse autoencoder features extracted at turn-boundary and pronoun-token positions and selected through a filtering pipeline for different depths. We characterize each surviving feature through its steering effects and activation distribution. translated_title: “我的名字众多”：通过稀疏自编码器解析助手及其人格的结构
translated_abstract: 摘要：arXiv:2608.07852v2 公告类型：替换 摘要：语言模型如何在内部表示说话者——是助手、指定的角色扮演人格，还是叙述的故事角色——这一问题仍未得到充分探索。我们使用一个包含用户表达情感文本及对应模型响应的数据集来研究说话者表示。我们将三种生成设置（助手、角色扮演和故事）分解为在轮次边界和代词标记位置提取的稀疏自编码器特征，并通过过滤流水线针对不同深度进行筛选。我们通过每个保留特征的引导效应和激活分布来表征其特性。我们的主要发现是，助手和角色扮演人格并非独立的替代选项：人格保留了与助手相关的特征核心，同时在各层中逐渐与其分化，从操作机制开始，进而涉及行为和风格特征。与此同时，生成的故事角色缺乏与助手相关的特征核心。
tldr: 本文通过稀疏自编码器揭示，语言模型中的角色扮演人格并非独立于助手，而是保留助手特征核心并逐层分化，而故事角色则完全缺乏该核心。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals via sparse autoencoders that roleplay personas in language models are not independent of the Assistant but retain its feature core while differentiating across layers, whereas story characters lack this core entirely.
